learning_outcomes.text: Use the basic properties of numerical sets and perform fundamental operations with them.
Operate and represent real functions of a real variable, obtain their limits, determine their continuity, calculate derivatives, and formulate and solve optimization problems.
Use the concepts of sequence and series, and use power series to represent functions.
State and apply the basic properties of real functions of several real variables. Obtain their limits, analyze continuity and differentiability, and solve optimization problems.
Solve Calculus problems using computational tools.

syllabus_topics: Topic 2: Real Functions of a Real Variable
Topic 3: Real Functions of Several Real Variables
Limits and continuity of real functions of two variables
Differentiability of real functions of several variables
Introduction to optimization of multi-variable functions
Topic 4: Sequences and Series of Real Numbers
Power Series. Convergence field of power series
teaching_methods: Virtual expository sessions (videos, presentations, instructional texts, self-assessment questionnaires)
In-person expository classes (doubt resolution, theoretical development, examples)
Virtual classroom practices (videos, questionnaires, forum participation)
In-person classroom practices (individual or group exercises and tasks)
Tutoring (Teams chat, Campus Virtual forums, personal virtual or in-person tutorials)
assessment_rules: For ordinary call, the final grade (NF) is calculated as 0.5 * NE + 0.2 * NPA + 0.2 * NL + 0.1 * NCV, where NE is (P1+P2)/2 if both partials were taken, otherwise it's the Written Exam. A minimum grade of 3.5 out of 10 is required for the Written Exam (NE) if taken as a single comprehensive test, and for Laboratory Practices (NL). The subject is passed if NF is 5 or greater. If minimums are not met, the grade will be the minimum of NF and 4.5. For extraordinary call, NF = 0.7 * NE + 0.1 * NCV + 0.2 * NL. A minimum grade of 3.5 out of 10 is required for the Written Exam (NE) and Laboratory Practices (NL).
